Think of a building. Before the walls go up, before the roof is placed, before anything else is built, workers lay a foundation — a solid base on which everything else rests. If the foundation is weak or missing, the whole building collapses. If it is strong, everything built on top of it is secure.

"Basis" is that foundation — but for non-physical things. It is the underlying idea, reason, principle, or fact on which everything else rests: a decision, a belief, an argument, a relationship, a system, or an action.

When you identify the basis of something, you are identifying its root — the thing it cannot exist without.
